Definition: from G102; to be unable, i.e. (passively) impossible:--be impossible.
BiblicalUsage: Adynateo means to be impossible — and in the New Testament it appears only twice, both times to say that nothing is impossible. Jesus tells His disciples that with mustard-seed faith nothing shall be impossible to them, and Gabriel tells Mary that with God nothing shall be impossible. The word exists in Scripture only to be denied: what cannot be done, God does.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that this word is pure gospel. Twice it appears, and twice it is attached to God's power breaking through human limits — a mountain moved by small faith, a child conceived by the Spirit. What I cannot do, God can, and this word says so twice.
